name: RAG & Retrieval Pipeline Security
description: Security assessment of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines. Covers access control on vector stores and retrieval, poisoning of retrieval corpora and embeddings, sensitive data leakage through retrieval (OWASP LLM08), and document-borne injection delivered via retrieved content. Poisoning of model training data belongs to AIML-ADV-POISON.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to RAG or retrieval pipeline security

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands how RAG pipelines ingest, embed, and retrieve content into model context
evidence: Can describe the ingestion, chunking, embedding, vector store, and retrieval stages of a RAG pipeline
Aware of vector and embedding weaknesses (LLM08) and retrieval-borne injection
Understands why retrieval must enforce the querying user's document permissions

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Can assess basic RAG pipeline risks under guidance
evidence: Tests whether a user can retrieve documents outside their authorisation through crafted queries
Plants a poisoned document in a lab corpus and observes its effect on answers
Reviews ingestion sources and vector store exposure with supervision

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses RAG pipelines for access control, poisoning, and leakage
evidence: Evaluates permission propagation from source systems through chunking into retrieval filters
Demonstrates corpus poisoning that steers retrieval ranking and model answers
Tests for sensitive data leakage across tenants, sessions, and embedding inversion
Produces findings with reproducible queries and pipeline-stage-specific mitigations

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex retrieval architectures; develops RAG assessment methodology; mentors others
evidence: Assesses hybrid search, multi-tenant vector stores, and agentic retrieval over live sources
Designs corpus integrity monitoring and provenance controls for ingestion pipelines
Develops tooling to measure poisoning success and retrieval leakage at scale
Reviews and calibrates RAG assessments across the team

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's RAG security assessment practice; publishes research
evidence: Established the lab's methodology for retrieval pipeline security assessment
Published research on retrieval poisoning, embedding leakage, or RAG access control
Trains teams on RAG security assessment
Contributes to external guidance on secure retrieval-augmented generation

assessment_methods.description: Against a multi-user lab RAG application, demonstrate cross-permission document retrieval and a corpus-poisoning attack that alters answers, then verify proposed fixes
Review a RAG assessment report for pipeline-stage coverage, access-control testing depth, and reproducibility of poisoning and leakage findings
